references.text: God sets His face against the one who eats blood; the same expression 'אֶתֵּן אֶת־פָּנַי' is used for God's judgment.
The prohibition against sacrificing children to Molech and profaning God's name, a direct parallel to the theme in 20:3.
Continuation of the same theme where God sets His face against those who follow Molech.
The priests must not profane God's name (לְחַלֵּל אֶת־שֵׁם), the same expression as in 20:3.
The prohibition against profaning God's holy name (וְלֹא תְחַלְּלוּ אֶת־שֵׁם קָדְשִׁי).
Ezekiel uses the same expression about setting His face against someone (וְנָתַתִּי פָנַי בָּאִישׁ הַהוּא).
Israel sacrificed their children to idols and profaned themselves, the same theme as child sacrifice.
They sacrificed their children to idols and profaned the sanctuary on that same day.
The people built high places for Molech in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom to sacrifice their children.
King Josiah defiled Topheth in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom so that no one could sacrifice children to Molech.
